components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical (单人旁) — 价 is about what people pay or the worth of things; also in 你, 他, 住.
介 (jiè) — near-sound hint — 价 is jià; 介 also sounds out 界 jiè and 阶 jiē.
亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 值 is worth.
直 (zhí) sounds exactly like 值; also 植 zhí and 置 zhì.

example.pinyin: Zhè fú huà hěn yǒu jiàzhí.
example.english: This painting is very valuable.
example.fact: 价值 usually shows up inside the set phrase 有价值 ("to have value," i.e. "valuable") rather than as a stand-alone adjective directly modifying a noun — to simply say something "is valuable," Chinese leans on 有价值 or the adjective 珍贵.

examples.hanzi: 这本书对学习汉语很有价值。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn shū duì xuéxí Hànyǔ hěn yǒu jiàzhí.
examples.english: This book is very valuable for learning Chinese.

examples.hanzi: 每个人的生命都有价值。
examples.pinyin: Měi ge rén de shēngmìng dōu yǒu jiàzhí.
examples.english: Everyone's life has value.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical, used for 仔 as "small creature or child", as in 牛仔 cowboy and 仔细 careful.
子 (zǐ) — same sound — 仔 is zǐ; 子 also means child, so sound and meaning agree.
纟 (silk, thread) — simplified 糸; thread is the classic fine thing, so 细 means thin, slender, then detailed — as in 线 line, 红 red.

example.pinyin: Qǐng zǐxì jiǎnchá zhè fèn hétong.
example.english: Please carefully check this contract.
example.fact: In 仔细, 仔 keeps its literary reading zǐ (rather than the colloquial zǎi heard in words like 仔仔, "kid"). 仔细 itself pairs naturally with verbs of perception and inspection (仔细看, 仔细听, 仔细检查) to mean "carefully, attentively," while its near-synonym 小心 leans toward physical caution around danger (小心台阶, "watch the steps") — a split between mental attentiveness and physical wariness that English "careful" doesn't separate.

examples.hanzi: 他做事很仔细。
examples.pinyin: Tā zuòshì hěn zǐxì.
examples.english: He is very careful in what he does.

examples.hanzi: 你仔细看看这张照片。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ zǐxì kànkan zhè zhāng zhàopiàn.
examples.english: Take a careful look at this photo.

components.note: 工 (work, craft) — craft and skill — clever handiwork; also in 左, 差.
丂 (kǎo) — near sound — 巧 qiǎo; 丂 also sounds out 考 kǎo and 烤 kǎo.
兄 (older brother) — the bottom part. Dictionary story: a weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄. A memory aid; the origin is debated. In names (杰克, 麦克) 克 is only sound.
十 (ten) — the top bar. Memory aid: ten times stronger than your brother 兄 — to overcome, as in 克服.
力 (strength) — an old picture of an arm or a plough, a tool of effort. As a radical it marks strength: 办, 助, 动, 努, 男.

example.pinyin: Tā zuì ài chī qiǎokèlì dàngāo.
example.english: She loves eating chocolate cake most.
example.fact: 巧克力 is a phonetic loanword transliterating English "chocolate," with each character chosen for sound rather than sense — 巧 ("clever"), 克 ("gram; to overcome"), 力 ("strength") add up to no coherent meaning at all, unlike a calque such as 电脑 ("electric brain" = computer) that translates the concept piece by piece.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢送她巧克力。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan sòng tā qiǎokèlì.
examples.english: I like giving her chocolate.

examples.hanzi: 这盒巧克力很甜。
examples.pinyin: Zhè hé qiǎokèlì hěn tián.
examples.english: This box of chocolates is very sweet.

components.note: 女 (woman) — a person kneeling with arms crossed; as a radical it heads many female and family words: 妈, 好, 姐.
土 (earth) — a green shoot pushing up from the ground: growth, birth, life. 生 also sounds out 性 xìng, 姓 xìng and 星 xīng.

example.pinyin: Bān lǐ yǒu shí gè nǚshēng.
example.english: There are ten girls in the class.
example.fact: 女生 literally frames someone by their status as a student (女 "female" + 生 "student, pupil," the same 生 as in 学生) — in casual speech it has broadened to mean simply "girl/young woman" even outside school, paralleling how 男生 ("male student") loosened into a general word for "guy."

examples.hanzi: 她是我们学校的女生。
examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒmen xuéxiào de nǚshēng.
examples.english: She is a female student at our school.

examples.hanzi: 女生宿舍在楼的左边。
examples.pinyin: Nǚshēng sùshè zài lóu de zuǒbiān.
examples.english: The girls' dormitory is on the left side of the building.

meanings: to carry on a shoulder pole

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 推; 挑 is to pick out by hand.
兆 (zhào) is a loose sound clue; same part in 跳 tiào, 桃 táo and 逃 táo.

example.pinyin: Nǐ bāng wǒ tiāo yí jiàn yīfu ba.
example.english: Help me pick out a piece of clothing.
example.fact: 挑 has two readings: tiāo (to choose, to carry on a pole) and tiǎo (to poke or provoke, as in 挑战, challenge). 挑食 means to be a picky eater and 挑剔 means to be fussy about details.

examples.hanzi: 我想挑一个大一点的西瓜。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng tiāo yí gè dà yìdiǎn de xīguā.
examples.english: I want to pick a slightly larger watermelon.

examples.hanzi: 他挑水上山，走了很远。
examples.pinyin: Tā tiāo shuǐ shàngshān, zǒule hěn yuǎn.
examples.english: He carried water up the mountain on a shoulder pole for a long way.

components.note: 辛 (xīn, bitter/pungent) — 辛 itself means hot and pungent, so 辣 is spicy hot, as in 辛辣; 辛 also appears in 辩 and 辟.
束 (shù) — only a loose sound hint (là vs shù); same part in 刺 cì.

example.hanzi: 这个菜太辣了，我吃不了。
example.pinyin: Zhège cài tài là le, wǒ chī bu liǎo.
example.english: This dish is too spicy, I can't eat it.
example.fact: 辣 describes chilli heat, and 麻辣 combines it with the numbing tingle (麻) of Sichuan pepper, a very Sichuan flavour pairing. It also describes stinging pain, as in 火辣辣 (burning hot), and 辣妹 is a "spicy girl" in slang.

examples.hanzi: 你喜欢吃辣的东西吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuan chī là de dōngxi ma?
examples.english: Do you like spicy food?

examples.hanzi: 我怕辣，请少放一点辣椒。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ pà là, qǐng shǎo fàng yìdiǎn làjiāo.
examples.english: I can't handle spice; please use less chili.

components.note: 互 (mutual) — the shape looks like two hooks locking into each other — a handy picture for "mutually" in 互相.
目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi hùxiāng bāngzhù.
example.english: We should help each other.
example.fact: 互相 is an adverb placed directly before the verb (互相帮助, "help each other") rather than after it the way English places "each other" — a word-order mismatch that often causes learners to misplace it in the sentence.

examples.hanzi: 他们互相介绍了自己。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen hùxiāng jièshàole zìjǐ.
examples.english: They introduced themselves to each other.

examples.hanzi: 朋友之间要互相理解。
examples.pinyin: Péngyou zhījiān yào hùxiāng lǐjiě.
examples.english: Friends should understand each other.

components.note: 刀 (knife, written 刂 on the right) — cutting, as in 分 divide, 刻 carve, 到 arrive.
七 (qī) is a close sound clue for qiē/qiè.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ píngguǒ qiē chéng xiǎo kuài.
example.english: Please cut the apple into small pieces.
example.fact: 切 has two readings: qiē (to cut) and qiè (close, earnest, as in 亲切 and 密切). The word 一切 ("everything") uses qiè, a typical learner trap.

examples.hanzi: 我用刀把肉切开。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yòng dāo bǎ ròu qiēkāi.
examples.english: I cut the meat open with a knife.

examples.hanzi: 请把洋葱切成细丝。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ yángcōng qiē chéng xìsī.
examples.english: Please cut the onion into thin strips.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 招 is to beckon with the hand.
召 (zhào) — near sound — 招 is zhāo; 召 also sounds out 照 zhào and 超 chāo.

example.pinyin: Tā xiàng wǒ zhāoshǒu.
example.english: He waved at me.
example.fact: 招手 is more general than English "wave": it covers beckoning, hailing a taxi, and waving hello. As a noun 招 means a move or trick (高招, a clever move), and 招聘 means to recruit staff.

examples.hanzi: 他在路边招手叫出租车。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài lùbiān zhāoshǒu jiào chūzūchē.
examples.english: He waved to hail a taxi by the roadside.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司正在招人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī zhèngzài zhāo rén.
examples.english: This company is hiring.

components.note: 火 (fire) — fire and heat: 灯, 烧, 爆; 炸 is to explode or to fry.
乍 (zhà) sounds exactly like 炸; also in 诈 zhà, 作 zuò, 昨 zuó.

example.pinyin: Qìqiú zhà le.
example.english: The balloon burst.
example.fact: 炸 has two readings: zhà (to explode) and zhá (to deep-fry, as in 炸鸡). 炸弹 is a bomb, and in slang 炸了 can mean someone is furious, a place is chaotic, or something is amazing.

examples.hanzi: 工厂发生了爆炸，炸坏了很多机器。
examples.pinyin: Gōngchǎng fāshēng le bàozhà, zhàhuài le hěn duō jīqì.
examples.english: An explosion at the factory wrecked many machines.

examples.hanzi: 他去买了炸鸡。
examples.pinyin: Tā qù mǎi le zhájī.
examples.english: He went to buy fried chicken.

components.note: 土 (earth) — marks soil, ground and earthen things, as in 地 ground, 城 city wall, 坏 broken; a wall was packed earth.
啬 (sè) is only a loose sound hint for qiáng.

example.pinyin: Qiáng shang guà zhe yì fú huà.
example.english: A painting hangs on the wall.
example.fact: The measure word depends on the wall: 一面墙 for a surface and 一堵墙 for a standing barrier. The proverb 隔墙有耳 ("walls have ears") warns that secrets can be overheard.

examples.hanzi: 他爬过了那堵墙。
examples.pinyin: Tā páguò le nà dǔ qiáng.
examples.english: He climbed over that wall.

examples.hanzi: 这面墙刚刷过，还没干。
examples.pinyin: Zhè miàn qiáng gāng shuāguo, hái méi gān.
examples.english: This wall has just been painted and is not dry yet.

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海, 汤; 流 is flowing water.
㐬 (liú) — same sound — 流 is liú; 㐬 also sounds out 琉 liú and 硫 liú.

example.pinyin: Hé shuǐ xiàng dōng liú.
example.english: The river flows east.
example.fact: 流 extends from water to anything that moves smoothly: 流利 (fluent), 流行 (fashionable, spreading like a current) and 交流 (to exchange). 流泪 means to shed tears and 流血 means to bleed.

examples.hanzi: 他难过得流下了眼泪。
examples.pinyin: Tā nánguò de liúxià le yǎnlèi.
examples.english: He was so sad that tears flowed down.

examples.hanzi: 这个消息很快就流传开了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi hěn kuài jiù liúchuán kāi le.
examples.english: This news spread quickly.

components.note: 厂 (shelter) — 厂 here is a simple shed or building; 厕 is the small room set apart for the toilet, as in 厕所.
则 (zé) — same final — 厕 is cè; 则 also sounds out 侧 cè and 测 cè, so all three share the sound.
斤 (axe) — cutting tools, as in 新 new and 斩 chop. 所 once echoed the sound of chopping; "place" and "that which" are later borrowed uses.

example.pinyin: Qǐngwèn, cèsuǒ zài nǎlǐ?
example.english: Excuse me, where is the restroom?
example.fact: 厕所 is the neutral, everyday word for "toilet/restroom"; more indirect terms like 洗手间 ("hand-washing room") or 卫生间 ("hygiene room") are often preferred in polite or formal settings, much as English speakers might ask for the "restroom" rather than name the fixture directly.

examples.hanzi: 我要去厕所。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yào qù cèsuǒ.
examples.english: I need to go to the toilet.

examples.hanzi: 这里的厕所很干净。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de cèsuǒ hěn gānjìng.
examples.english: The toilets here are very clean.

components.note: 無 (traditional) — began as a person dancing with ornaments (same root as 舞). 'None' is a borrowed sense; 无 is an old variant of 無 and the shape does not explain it.
辛 (bitter, harsh) — 辛 hints at hardship and punishment, as in 辣 spicy, 辩; 辜 is guilt, in 无辜 innocent.
古 (gǔ) — same sound, different tone — 辜 is gū; 古 also sounds out 姑 gū and 估 gū.

example.hanzi: 很多无辜的人在这场灾难中受伤。
example.pinyin: Hěn duō wúgū de rén zài zhè chǎng zāinàn zhōng shòushāng.
example.english: Many innocent people were injured in this disaster.
example.fact: 无辜 describes freedom from wrongdoing or blame in a serious, often legal or moral context (无辜的受害者, "an innocent victim") — for the lighter, everyday sense of "innocent" as in a child's unworldly look, Chinese instead reaches for 天真 ("naive, innocent").

examples.hanzi: 法官相信他是无辜的。
examples.pinyin: Fǎguān xiāngxìn tā shì wúgū de.
examples.english: The judge believes he is innocent.

examples.hanzi: 他不想让无辜的孩子受苦。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎng ràng wúgū de háizi shòukǔ.
examples.english: He doesn't want innocent children to suffer.

components.note: 彳 (step, walk) — left-step radical, like 行 in 径, 往, 德; 彻 is passing all the way through.
切 (qiē, qiè) — loose hint only — 彻 is chè, and the old form of 彻 was different, so the sound clue today is weak.
广 (shelter) — buildings, as in 店 shop, 床 bed, 度 degree; 底 is the base of a house.
氐 (dī) is a close sound clue for dǐ; also in 低 dī and 抵 dǐ.

example.pinyin: Zhè cì gǎigé fēicháng chèdǐ.
example.english: This reform is very thorough.
example.fact: 彻底 can sit on either side of the verb it modifies — before it as an adverb (彻底解决, "resolve thoroughly") or after 得 as a complement (解决得彻底, "resolved thoroughly") — letting the same word describe how completely an action was carried out from either position.

examples.hanzi: 他把房间彻底打扫了一遍。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ fángjiān chèdǐ dǎsǎole yí biàn.
examples.english: He cleaned the room thoroughly once.

examples.hanzi: 我彻底忘记了这件事。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ chèdǐ wàngjìle zhè jiàn shì.
examples.english: I completely forgot about this.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 搭 is to put up or join.
荅 (dā) sounds exactly like 搭; also in 答 dá.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen dā huǒchē qù Shànghǎi.
example.english: We are taking the train to Shanghai.
example.fact: 搭 means to catch a ride: 搭火车, 搭飞机; in mainland usage 坐 is more common for "to ride". It also means to pair things up: 搭配 (to match, as clothes or food) and 搭档 (a partner).

examples.hanzi: 我们搭出租车去吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen dā chūzūchē qù ba.
examples.english: Let's take a taxi.

examples.hanzi: 他们在院子里搭了一个棚子。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài yuànzi lǐ dā le yí gè péngzi.
examples.english: They built a shed in the yard.

components.note: 目 (eye) — looking; an eye turned on a tree 木, hence to look at, and mutually looking: "each other". 相 also gives 想 xiǎng, 箱 xiāng and 湘 xiāng.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen yào hùxiāng bāngzhù.
example.english: We should help each other.
example.fact: 相 as xiāng is an adverb meaning "mutually" in 相信, 相爱, 相同. As xiàng it means appearance or photograph: 照相 (to take a photo), 相片. Same character, different tone, different meaning.

examples.hanzi: 这两个人长得相像。
examples.pinyin: Zhè liǎng gè rén zhǎng de xiāngxiàng.
examples.english: These two people look alike.

examples.hanzi: 我们相信你，你一定可以的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xiāngxìn nǐ, nǐ yídìng kěyǐ de.
examples.english: We believe in you; you can definitely do it.

components.note: 木 (wood) — originally 權, the sliding weight of a steelyard scale: weighing, then power; 又 is just a simplification stand-in.

example.hanzi: 每个人都有说话的权利。
example.pinyin: Měi ge rén dōu yǒu shuōhuà de quánlì.
example.english: Everyone has the right to speak.
example.fact: 权利 (right, entitlement) and 权力 (power, authority) are both pronounced quánlì, which makes them an easy pair to confuse in listening. 权 also appears in 人权 (human rights), 版权 (copyright) and 权威 (authority).

examples.hanzi: 每个人都有投票的权利。
examples.pinyin: Měi gè rén dōu yǒu tóupiào de quánlì.
examples.english: Everyone has the right to vote.

examples.hanzi: 这个孩子的权力不大，他只是班长。
examples.pinyin: Zhège háizi de quánlì bú dà, tā zhǐshì bānzhǎng.
examples.english: This kid doesn't have much authority; he is only the class monitor.

components.note: 羽 (feather, wing) — marks wings and flying, as in 翅 wing, 翔 soar; 翻 is flipping like wings, then turning over.
番 (fān) — same sound: 翻 fān. 番 also sounds out 蕃 fān and 幡 fān.

example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ shū fān dào dì shí yè.
example.english: Please turn to page ten of the book.
example.fact: 翻 is to flip or turn over, as in 翻页 (turn a page) and 翻身 (turn over in bed). 翻译 (to translate) literally means turning one language over to another, and 翻脸 means to suddenly turn hostile.

examples.hanzi: 他翻了翻书，没有找到那一页。
examples.pinyin: Tā fān le fān shū, méiyǒu zhǎodào nà yí yè.
examples.english: He flipped through the book and couldn't find that page.

examples.hanzi: 你能把这篇文章翻成英文吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng bǎ zhè piān wénzhāng fān chéng Yīngwén ma?
examples.english: Can you translate this article into English?

components.note: 扌 (hand) — hand radical — 摆 is to arrange or swing with the hands.
罢 (bà) — near sound — 摆 is bǎi, matching 罢.

example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang bǎi zhe hěn duō shuǐguǒ.
example.english: Lots of fruit is laid out on the table.
example.fact: 摆 suggests putting things out in an orderly or visible way: 摆摊 (set up a stall), 摆桌子 (to lay a table). 摆手 means waving the hand, which in China often means "no" or "stop"; 摆脱 means to shake off.

examples.hanzi: 请把椅子摆好。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ yǐzi bǎi hǎo.
examples.english: Please arrange the chairs properly.

examples.hanzi: 他在桌上摆了几盘菜。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài zhuōshang bǎile jǐ pán cài.
examples.english: He set several dishes on the table.

components.note: 辶 (walk) — movement, as in 这, 近, 送: 过 is to pass or cross.
寸 here replaces 咼 (guō) of the traditional 過, so it is not a sound clue; 咼 survives in 锅 guō and 祸 huò.
禾 (grain) — grain radical — 程 first meant to measure grain, hence standard, then course and journey; also in 种, 秋, 稿.
呈 (chéng) — same sound — 程 is chéng; 呈 also sounds out 逞 chěng.

example.hanzi: 学习语言是一个漫长的过程。
example.pinyin: Xuéxí yǔyán shì yí gè màncháng de guòchéng.
example.english: Learning a language is a long process.
example.fact: 过程 combines 过 ("to pass through, cross") with 程 ("a measured stage, journey") — its image of "the stages passed through" lines up closely with English "process," itself from Latin procedere, "to go forward": two unrelated languages arriving at a similar journey metaphor for the same abstract idea.

examples.hanzi: 这个过程很复杂。
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge guòchéng hěn fùzá.
examples.english: This process is complicated.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢做饭的过程。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan zuòfàn de guòchéng.
examples.english: I enjoy the process of cooking.

components.note: 上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.
欠 (open mouth, lack) — yawning, breathing and wanting: 歌 song, 欢 joy, 吹 blow; 次 also sounds out 资 zī and 瓷 cí.

example.hanzi: 上次我们去的那家餐厅很好吃。
example.pinyin: Shàngcì wǒmen qù de nà jiā cāntīng hěn hǎochī.
example.english: That restaurant we went to last time was delicious.
example.fact: 上次 uses 上 ("up, previous," as in 上个月 "last month") rather than 前 ("before, front") to mark "last/previous" — Chinese consistently treats earlier events as "up" and later ones as "down" (下次, "next time"), the mirror image of English's own "up next."

examples.hanzi: 上次你说的那本书叫什么？
examples.pinyin: Shàng cì nǐ shuō de nà běn shū jiào shénme?
examples.english: What was the book you mentioned last time called?

examples.hanzi: 上次考试我只得了六十分。
examples.pinyin: Shàng cì kǎoshì wǒ zhǐ déle liùshí fēn.
examples.english: Last time on the exam I only got sixty points.

components.note: 申 (lightning) — 申 pictured a flash of lightning; the later character 电 grew out of it, and 申 stays as the phonetic in 伸 shēn, 神 shén and 绅 shēn.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and asking: 说, 谢, 谈; 请 is to ask politely.
青 (qīng) sounds like 请 (tone differs); same part in 清, 情, 晴, 精, 静.

example.hanzi: 我在申请一所大学的研究生项目。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zài shēnqǐng yì suǒ dàxué de yánjiūshēng xiàngmù.
example.english: I'm applying to a university's graduate program.
example.fact: 申请 combines 申 ("to state, extend," from an old pictograph of a lightning bolt) with 请 ("to request") — literally "to formally state a request," a compositional image well suited to its modern bureaucratic sense of filing an application.

examples.hanzi: 我想申请一张银行卡。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng shēnqǐng yì zhāng yínhángkǎ.
examples.english: I'd like to apply for a bank card.

examples.hanzi: 他申请了一份新工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā shēnqǐngle yí fèn xīn gōngzuò.
examples.english: He applied for a new job.

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
上 (above) — a mark above a line, the mirror of 下 below.

example.hanzi: 我手上正拿着一杯咖啡。
example.pinyin: Wǒ shǒu shang zhèng ná zhe yì bēi kāfēi.
example.english: I'm currently holding a cup of coffee in my hand.
example.fact: 手上 extends past its literal sense ("in one's hand") into an idiomatic one meaning "currently in one's possession or charge" (手上的工作, "the work on my plate right now") — much like English "on hand" or "in hand" stretches from a literal grip to a sense of immediate availability or responsibility.

examples.hanzi: 我手上有两张电影票。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shǒu shang yǒu liǎng zhāng diànyǐngpiào.
examples.english: I have two movie tickets in hand.

examples.hanzi: 你手上拿的是什么？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shǒu shang ná de shì shénme?
examples.english: What are you holding in your hand?

components.note: 土 (earth) — soil and land: 地, 场, 坏; 压 is earth pressed down under a cliff 厂.

example.pinyin: Tā de yālì hěn dà.
example.english: He is under a lot of pressure.
example.fact: 压力 means both physical pressure and mental stress. 压岁钱 is the red-envelope money given to children at the New Year. 血压 is blood pressure, and the colloquial 压根儿 (yàgēnr) means "at all" in negative statements.

examples.hanzi: 别压着我的书包。
examples.pinyin: Bié yā zhe wǒ de shūbāo.
examples.english: Don't press down on my bag.

examples.hanzi: 他的肩膀被重物压疼了。
examples.pinyin: Tā de jiānbǎng bèi zhòngwù yā téng le.
examples.english: His shoulder hurt from the heavy load.

components.note: 火 (fire) — roasting over flames; also in 烧 burn, 煮 cook.
考 (kǎo) gives the exact sound; it also sounds out 拷 kǎo and 铐 kào.

example.pinyin: Wǒmen wǎnshang kǎo yú ba.
example.english: Let's grill fish this evening.
example.fact: 烤 is used for roasting, baking and barbecuing, so 烤鸭 is roast duck, 烤箱 is an oven and 烤火 means to warm oneself by a fire. 烤 can also describe burning in the sun: 被太阳烤着.

examples.hanzi: 他喜欢烤面包，每天早上都吃。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan kǎo miànbāo, měitiān zǎoshang dōu chī.
examples.english: He likes toasting bread and eats it every morning.

examples.hanzi: 在火边烤一烤，手就暖和了。
examples.pinyin: Zài huǒ biān kǎo yi kǎo, shǒu jiù nuǎnhuo le.
examples.english: Warm your hands by the fire and they'll feel better.

components.note: 讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and asking: 说, 谢, 谈; 请 is to ask politely.
青 (qīng) sounds like 请 (tone differs); same part in 清, 情, 晴, 精, 静.
求 (seek) — the original picture of a fur coat (裘 qiú adds 衣); "seek, request" is a borrowed use. 求 sounds out 球 qiú and 救 jiù.

example.pinyin: Tā xiàng lǎoshī tíchūle qǐngqiú.
example.english: He made a request to the teacher.
example.fact: 请求 sits at a more formal, deliberate register than the everyday verb 请 ("please, to ask/invite") — 请求 turns up in official, written, or emotionally weighted contexts (请求帮助, "to request help"), while a casual ask usually just uses 请 or 问.

examples.hanzi: 她请求大家的原谅。
examples.pinyin: Tā qǐngqiú dàjiā de yuánliàng.
examples.english: She asked for everyone's forgiveness.

examples.hanzi: 这是一个很小的请求，你能帮我吗？
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí ge hěn xiǎo de qǐngqiú, nǐ néng bāng wǒ ma?
examples.english: This is a small request, can you help me?

components.note: 圣 (holy) — traditional 聖 had an ear 耳 and a mouth 口: the sage who listens and speaks wisely.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — speech: 说, 话, 请; 诞 first meant big talk, then birth and birthday.
延 (yán) is only a loose sound hint for dàn.
艹 stands in for 竹 (bamboo) in the traditional 節, bamboo joints: sections, then festivals and knots.

example.hanzi: 我们全家一起过圣诞节。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen quánjiā yìqǐ guò Shèngdànjié.
example.english: Our whole family celebrates Christmas together.
example.fact: 圣诞节 literally means "holy birth festival" (圣 "holy" + 诞 "birth" + 节 "festival") — a calque translating the Christian meaning of Christmas directly into Chinese, rather than transliterating the English sound the way 巧克力 and 好莱坞 (also in this batch) do.

examples.hanzi: 圣诞节前，商店里很热闹。
examples.pinyin: Shèngdànjié qián, shāngdiàn lǐ hěn rènao.
examples.english: Before Christmas the shops are very lively.

examples.hanzi: 圣诞节快到了，我想买一些礼物。
examples.pinyin: Shèngdànjié kuài dào le, wǒ xiǎng mǎi yìxiē lǐwù.
examples.english: Christmas is coming and I want to buy some gifts.

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — cliffs and rocks, as in 厅 hall, 厚 thick: a spring flowing from a cliff.
泉 (spring) — water from the rock: the source (源 yuán adds 氵 later); 原 is source, origin.

example.pinyin: Yuánlái shì nǐ a!
example.english: So it was you!
example.fact: 原来 can mean "originally" or "so it turns out" in a realization like 原来是你. 原 is the older form of 源 (source) and also appears in 原因 (reason), 原谅 (to forgive) and 草原 (grassland).

examples.hanzi: 这是我原来的名字。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ yuánlái de míngzi.
examples.english: This is my original name.

examples.hanzi: 请按原价付钱。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng àn yuánjià fùqián.
examples.english: Please pay the original price.

components.note: 木 (tree) — 某 first named a sour tree fruit; now it means a certain, unnamed one. It sounds out 媒 méi, 煤 méi and 谋 móu.
此 (cǐ) is a loose sound clue for xiē; 此 also sounds out 紫 zǐ and 雌 cí. 些 is the plural-ish "some, a few".

example.hanzi: 某些人对这个消息表示怀疑。
example.pinyin: Mǒuxiē rén duì zhège xiāoxi biǎoshì huáiyí.
example.english: Certain people are skeptical about this news.
example.fact: 某些 deliberately avoids naming who or what is meant — like English "certain people," it hedges in a way that implies the speaker knows specifics but is choosing to withhold them, often to sound diplomatic or quietly pointed.

examples.hanzi: 某些学生的成绩进步很快。
examples.pinyin: Mǒuxiē xuésheng de chéngjì jìnbù hěn kuài.
examples.english: The grades of some students improved quickly.

examples.hanzi: 这种水果在某些地方很贵。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng shuǐguǒ zài mǒuxiē dìfang hěn guì.
examples.english: This fruit is expensive in some places.

components.note: 人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.
民 (people) — one old theory sees an eye pierced by a pointed tool, a mark of those with no rights; the meaning "ordinary people" is what to remember.

example.hanzi: 人民的生活水平不断提高。
example.pinyin: Rénmín de shēnghuó shuǐpíng búduàn tígāo.
example.english: The people's standard of living keeps improving.
example.fact: 人民 carries a more collective, political register than the plain word 人 ("person/people") — it's the term chosen for a nation's citizenry as a political body, as in 人民共和国 ("People's Republic") and 人民币 ("the people's currency," i.e. RMB), rather than for people as individuals in everyday speech.

examples.hanzi: 人民的生活越来越好。
examples.pinyin: Rénmín de shēnghuó yuè lái yuè hǎo.
examples.english: The people's lives are getting better and better.

examples.hanzi: 人民银行是中国的中央银行。
examples.pinyin: Rénmín Yínháng shì Zhōngguó de zhōngyāng yínháng.
examples.english: The People's Bank is China's central bank.

components.note: 心 (heart) — feelings: 想, 思, 感, 怕; 恐 is fear.
巩 (gǒng) is a near sound match (-ong).
忄 (heart) — heart radical for feelings, as in 怕 afraid, 情, 慌; 惧 is the feeling of fear.
具 (jù) — same sound — 具 sounds out 俱 jù and 惧 jù.

example.hanzi: 她克服了对失败的恐惧。
example.pinyin: Tā kèfú le duì shībài de kǒngjù.
example.english: She overcame her fear of failure.
example.fact: 恐惧 doubles up two "heart" radicals — 心 in 恐, 忄 in 惧 — fitting for a formal, written-register word for deep dread; everyday spoken Chinese reaches for the plainer 怕 instead ("我怕黑" rather than the more literary "我对黑暗感到恐惧").

examples.hanzi: 黑暗中,孩子心里充满了恐惧。
examples.pinyin: Hēi'àn zhōng, háizi xīnli chōngmǎn le kǒngjù.
examples.english: In the dark, the child was filled with fear.

examples.hanzi: 他从不让恐惧影响自己的决定。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng bù ràng kǒngjù yǐngxiǎng zìjǐ de juédìng.
examples.english: He never lets fear affect his decisions.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 话.
炎 (yán) is a close sound clue for tán; 炎 also sounds out 淡 dàn and 痰 tán.
讠 (speech, simplified 言) — talking and discussion: 说, 议, 谈; 论 is debate and theory.
仑 (lún) gives the sound; same part in 轮 lún and 伦 lún.

example.hanzi: 我们在谈论明天的计划。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen zài tánlùn míngtiān de jìhuà.
example.english: We are discussing tomorrow's plan.
example.fact: 谈论 is a transitive verb that takes its topic directly as an object — 谈论这个问题 ("discuss this issue") — with no preposition needed, unlike English "talk about," where "about" can't simply be dropped.

examples.hanzi: 你们在谈论什么,这么开心?
examples.pinyin: Nǐmen zài tánlùn shénme, zhème kāixīn?
examples.english: What are you talking about that's making you so happy?

examples.hanzi: 大家都在谈论这部新电影。
examples.pinyin: Dàjiā dōu zài tánlùn zhè bù xīn diànyǐng.
examples.english: Everyone is talking about this new movie.

components.note: 口 (mouth) — speech, as in 吃, 唱, 问: an order is spoken.
令 (lìng, order) is a close sound clue for mìng; 令 also in 领 lǐng, 冷 lěng and 零 líng.
辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 运 is to move, then to be moved by luck.
云 (yún) is a near sound match for yùn.

example.hanzi: 他相信自己能改变命运。
example.pinyin: Tā xiāngxìn zìjǐ néng gǎibiàn mìngyùn.
example.english: He believes he can change his own fate.
example.fact: 运 alone already means "luck, fortune" (as in 幸运, "lucky"), while 命 separately means "life, decree" — 命运 fuses a person's "life-decree" with "fortune" into one grander idea of overarching destiny, bigger in scope than the everyday luck of 运气.

examples.hanzi: 没有人能决定自己的命运。
examples.pinyin: Méiyǒu rén néng juédìng zìjǐ de mìngyùn.
examples.english: No one can decide their own fate.

examples.hanzi: 命运让我们在这座城市相遇。
examples.pinyin: Mìngyùn ràng wǒmen zài zhè zuò chéngshì xiāngyù.
examples.english: Fate brought us together in this city.

components.note: 小 (small) — three small dots, tiny grains. As a radical it appears in 少 few, 尖 sharp.
纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 线; 组 is to weave threads together, so to form a group.
且 (qiě) loosely hints at zǔ; 组 sounds exactly like 祖 zǔ and 阻 zǔ, same part.

example.hanzi: 老师把学生分成了五个小组。
example.pinyin: Lǎoshī bǎ xuésheng fēnchéng le wǔ gè xiǎozǔ.
example.english: The teacher divided the students into five groups.
example.fact: 组 carries the silk-thread radical 纟 because it originally meant "to weave, to arrange" — the same image of interlacing strands behind 组织 ("organization"), with 小组 simply naming a smaller such unit inside a larger body.

examples.hanzi: 我们这个小组一共有六个人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhège xiǎozǔ yígòng yǒu liù ge rén.
examples.english: Our group has six people in total.

examples.hanzi: 请各小组把讨论的结果写下来。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng gè xiǎozǔ bǎ tǎolùn de jiéguǒ xiě xiàlái.
examples.english: Please have each group write down its discussion results.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — the vertical stroke 丨 is the string being drawn back on a bow — 引 is to pull, then to attract and to cite.
走 (walk, run) — movement, as in 赶 chase, 超 surpass, 越 cross over; 起 is to rise or get up.
己 (jǐ) is a loose sound clue for qǐ; 己 also sounds out 记 jì and 纪 jì.

example.hanzi: 这个消息引起了很多人的注意。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiāoxi yǐnqǐ le hěn duō rén de zhùyì.
example.english: This news drew a lot of people's attention.
example.fact: 引起 almost always takes an abstract noun as its object — attention (注意), interest (兴趣), controversy (争议) — rather than a concrete physical event; for a plainer physical cause-and-effect, Chinese reaches for 导致 or 造成 instead, both of which lean more negative in tone.

examples.hanzi: 大雨引起了城市里的交通堵塞。
examples.pinyin: Dàyǔ yǐnqǐ le chéngshì lǐ de jiāotōng dǔsè.
examples.english: The heavy rain caused traffic jams in the city.

examples.hanzi: 这个问题引起了老师的重视。
examples.pinyin: Zhège wèntí yǐnqǐ le lǎoshī de zhòngshì.
examples.english: This problem caught the teacher's attention.

components.note: 发 (send out, hair) — two characters merged in simplified writing: 發 fā "emit, issue" and 髮 fà "hair" (头发).
尸 (body/roof) — the top-left cover, as in 层 and 局. In 展 it works like a cover over cloth that is spread out; memory aid, shape is partly simplified.
衣 (clothing) — a bit of this sits inside 展. Dictionary story: laying out clothes to display them, hence 'unfold, exhibit' in 展示.

example.hanzi: 这个城市这些年发展得很快。
example.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì zhèxiē nián fāzhǎn de hěn kuài.
example.english: This city has developed very quickly in recent years.
example.fact: 展 alone already means "to unfold, to spread out" (built from the image of clothing laid out for display, 尸+衣) — 发展 literally combines "to send forth" with "to unfold," a vivid image of outward expansion that maps neatly onto its modern sense of economic or personal "development."

examples.hanzi: 我希望公司能有更好的发展。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xīwàng gōngsī néng yǒu gèng hǎo de fāzhǎn.
examples.english: I hope the company can have better development.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们要在学习和运动上均衡发展。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen yào zài xuéxí hé yùndòng shàng jūnhéng fāzhǎn.
examples.english: Children should develop in a balanced way in both study and sports.

components.note: 刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 切, 刻, 到: a blade splits.
八 (eight) — originally two lines pulling apart: divide. 分 also gives 份 fèn, 粉 fěn and 纷 fēn.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.hanzi: 每个水分子都由两个氢原子和一个氧原子组成。
example.pinyin: Měi gè shuǐ fēnzǐ dōu yóu liǎng gè qīng yuánzǐ hé yí gè yǎng yuánzǐ zǔchéng.
example.english: Every water molecule is made up of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
example.fact: 分子 has two separate CEDICT readings for the same two characters: fēnzǐ, "molecule" (or "numerator" in math), is the ordinary standalone reading, while fènzǐ, "a member of a group," surfaces only bound inside words like 恐怖分子 ("terrorist") and 知识分子 ("intellectual") — easy to conflate since the characters and tones look almost identical on the page.

examples.hanzi: 科学家正在研究这种分子的结构。
examples.pinyin: Kēxuéjiā zhèngzài yánjiū zhè zhǒng fēnzǐ de jiégòu.
examples.english: Scientists are studying the structure of this molecule.

examples.hanzi: 这个分数的分子是三,分母是五。
examples.pinyin: Zhège fēnshù de fēnzǐ shì sān, fēnmǔ shì wǔ.
examples.english: The numerator of this fraction is three and the denominator is five.

components.note: 白 (white, bright) — gives sound to 拍 pāi, 怕 pà, 伯 bó and 泊 bó. Meaning: white, clear, plain, hence "明白" understand.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 那个白人男子是我们的新老师。
example.pinyin: Nàge báirén nánzǐ shì wǒmen de xīn lǎoshī.
example.english: That white man is our new teacher.
example.fact: 白人 follows a simple, transparent pattern shared by 黑人 ("Black person") and 亚洲人 ("Asian person") — colour or origin term plus 人 ("person") — one of Mandarin's most predictable ways to name an ethnicity.

examples.hanzi: 这位白人游客想学说中文。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi báirén yóukè xiǎng xué shuō Zhōngwén.
examples.english: This white tourist wants to learn to speak Chinese.

examples.hanzi: 街上走过来一个年轻的白人女孩。
examples.pinyin: Jiē shang zǒu guòlái yí ge niánqīng de báirén nǚhái.
examples.english: A young white girl walked toward us along the street.

components.note: 忄 (heart, 竖心旁) — feelings and mind: 怕, 情, 快; 惊 is a startled heart.
京 (jīng) sounds exactly like 惊; also in 鲸 jīng and 景 jǐng.
讠 (speech) — simplified 言 (speech), as in 说, 话, 读; 讶 is the exclamation of surprise.
牙 (yá) — near sound — 讶 is yà; 牙 also sounds out 芽 yá.

example.hanzi: 听到这个消息,他感到非常惊讶。
example.pinyin: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā gǎndào fēicháng jīngyà.
example.english: Hearing this news, he felt very astonished.
example.fact: Both characters point to a physical reaction — 惊 carries the heart radical 忄 for an emotional jolt, and 讶 carries the speech radical 讠 for the exclamation that jolt produces — together painting astonishment as something felt in the chest and voiced aloud.

examples.hanzi: 看到他突然出现,我很惊讶。
examples.pinyin: Kàndào tā tūrán chūxiàn, wǒ hěn jīngyà.
examples.english: I was surprised to see him suddenly appear.

examples.hanzi: 她惊讶地问:“你怎么会在这里?”
examples.pinyin: Tā jīngyà de wèn: "Nǐ zěnme huì zài zhèlǐ?"
examples.english: She asked in surprise, "How come you're here?"

components.note: 火 (fire) — marks fire and light, as in 烧, 燃, 热; 灯 is a lamp.
丁 (dīng) hints at the sound: 灯 dēng is close.

example.pinyin: Qǐng guān dēng.
example.english: Please turn off the light.
example.fact: 灯 has the measure word 盏: 一盏灯. 开灯 and 关灯 are "turn on / off the light". 红绿灯 is the traffic light, and the Lantern Festival (元宵节) is also called 灯节.

examples.hanzi: 天黑了，请开灯。
examples.pinyin: Tiān hēi le, qǐng kāidēng.
examples.english: It's dark; please turn on the light.

examples.hanzi: 街上挂满了红灯笼。
examples.pinyin: Jiē shang guà mǎn le hóng dēnglong.
examples.english: The street is hung with red lanterns.

components.note: 木 (wood) — wood radical — tables are wooden furniture, like 椅 chair, 板 board.
卓 (zhuō) — same sound as 桌 zhuō — a clear sound clue.
子 (child) — a picture of a baby with arms outstretched and legs bundled. As a suffix (孩子, 房子) it is a light noun ending.

example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shàng fàngzhe yì běn shū.
example.english: There's a book lying on the table.
example.fact: 子 here is a fully "bleached" noun suffix — it contributes no meaning of its own (unlike in 孩子, where 子 still echoes "child") and simply marks 桌 as a countable, concrete noun, the same grammatical role it plays in 椅子 ("chair") and 杯子 ("cup").

examples.hanzi: 请把桌子擦干净。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhuōzi cā gānjìng.
examples.english: Please wipe the table clean.

examples.hanzi: 我们家的桌子很大,能坐八个人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jiā de zhuōzi hěn dà, néng zuò bā ge rén.
examples.english: Our table is big and seats eight people.

components.note: 巴 (bā) — 巴 gives the sound bā in 爸 bà, 吧 ba, 把 bǎ and 疤 bā, so it is a useful sound clue.

example.pinyin: Wǒ bābude mǎshàng huí jiā.
example.english: I can't wait to get home.
example.fact: 巴不得 is a fixed phrase meaning "to be dying to", and it is used for things the speaker eagerly wants. Elsewhere 巴 serves as a soft suffix in 嘴巴 (mouth) and 尾巴 (tail), and as the transliteration in 巴士 (bus).

examples.hanzi: 孩子巴不得马上放假。
examples.pinyin: Háizi bābude mǎshàng fàngjià.
examples.english: The child can't wait for the holidays to start.

examples.hanzi: 孩子趴在妈妈身上，紧紧地巴着她。
examples.pinyin: Háizi pā zài māma shēn shang, jǐnjǐn de bā zhe tā.
examples.english: The child lay on his mother, clinging tightly to her.

components.note: 比 (bǐ) — near sound — 毕 is bì; 比 also sounds out 毙 bì, so the shared syllable bì is easy to remember.
Memory aid: 业 looks like a row of upright posts on a base, like a shop sign or an old tool stand; 'business/trade' is the extended meaning. Origin is unclear, so no firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 她今年夏天从大学毕业。
example.pinyin: Tā jīnnián xiàtiān cóng dàxué bìyè.
example.english: She will graduate from university this summer.
example.fact: 毕业 is a verb-object compound built from 毕 ("to finish") plus 业 ("course of study") — literally "to finish one's studies" — which is why it's grammatically intransitive: you say 从大学毕业 ("graduate from university"), never 毕业大学.

examples.hanzi: 你什么时候毕业?
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shénme shíhou bìyè?
examples.english: When do you graduate?

examples.hanzi: 他毕业以后在一家银行工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā bìyè yǐhòu zài yì jiā yínháng gōngzuò.
examples.english: After graduating, he worked at a bank.

components.note: 纟 (thread, simplified 糸) — silk and cord: 红, 给, 线; 练 first meant boiling silk to soften it, then practice.
柬 (jiǎn) is a loose sound clue; same part in 炼 liàn and 简 jiǎn.
习 (practice) — simplified from 習, a young bird 羽 flapping its wings again and again to learn to fly.

example.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān dōu liànxí xiě Hànzì.
example.english: I practice writing Chinese characters every day.
example.fact: 练 alone traces back to boiling and whitening raw silk thread until it becomes smooth and refined — 练习 extends that image of repeated refinement to any skill honed through repetition, from a musical instrument to a foreign language.

examples.hanzi: 为了考试,我们要多做练习。
examples.pinyin: Wèile kǎoshì, wǒmen yào duō zuò liànxí.
examples.english: To prepare for the exam, we need to do more exercises.

examples.hanzi: 她正在练习弹钢琴。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhèngzài liànxí tán gāngqín.
examples.english: She is practicing the piano.

components.note: 灬 (fire dots) — fire and heat: 热, 点, 煮, 照; 黑 is soot and smoke from a flame.
日 (sun) — sun radical — dark is the lack of daylight; compare 明 bright, 晚 evening.
音 (yīn) — loose sound hint — 暗 is àn; 音 also sounds out 谙 ān.

example.pinyin: Yèwǎn de sēnlín yí piàn hēi'àn.
example.english: The forest at night is pitch dark.
example.fact: 黑暗 doubles up two independent "dark" characters — 黑 (soot blackening a face over a fire) and 暗 (the sun 日 obscured) — and unlike the more physical 黑 alone, 黑暗 extends naturally into a figurative "dark" as well, as in 黑暗的时代 ("a dark age").

examples.hanzi: 突然停电了,房间里一片黑暗。
examples.pinyin: Tūrán tíngdiàn le, fángjiān lǐ yí piàn hēi'àn.
examples.english: The power suddenly went out and the room was pitch dark.

examples.hanzi: 他不想回到那段黑暗的日子。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎng huídào nà duàn hēi'àn de rìzi.
examples.english: He doesn't want to go back to those dark days.

components.note: 木 (tree) — wood, as in 树, 林, 桌; the older meaning was a wooden mechanism.
几 (jī) gives the exact sound; also in 饥 jī and 肌 jī.
土 (earth) — ground and place, as in 地, 城, 坐: a field or open space.
昜 (yáng) is the traditional sound part, a loose clue for chǎng; the same part is in 汤 tāng, 扬 yáng and 肠 cháng.

example.hanzi: 我们明天早上八点到机场。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān zǎoshang bā diǎn dào jīchǎng.
example.english: We'll arrive at the airport at eight tomorrow morning.
example.fact: 场 (a flat open area of ground, from 土 "earth") is Mandarin's general term for a large purpose-built venue — the same character turns up in 广场 ("public square") and 停车场 ("parking lot") — with 机场 simply naming the "ground" set aside for aircraft (机).

examples.hanzi: 去机场的路上堵车了。
examples.pinyin: Qù jīchǎng de lùshang dǔchē le.
examples.english: There was a traffic jam on the way to the airport.

examples.hanzi: 飞机明天下午从机场起飞。
examples.pinyin: Fēijī míngtiān xiàwǔ cóng jīchǎng qǐfēi.
examples.english: The plane takes off from the airport tomorrow afternoon.

meanings: publicly funded institution, enterprise or foundation

components.note: 彐 (hand-like part) — 事 is usually explained as a hand holding a tool or tally, 'handling business' — a hedged reading, not certain.
史 (history, scribe) — shares an ancient root with 事: a hand holding a recording tool. Both are about handling official 'matters'.
Memory aid: 业 looks like a row of upright posts on a base, like a shop sign or an old tool stand; 'business/trade' is the extended meaning. Origin is unclear, so no firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 他把所有的时间都花在了事业上。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ suǒyǒu de shíjiān dōu huā zài le shìyè shàng.
example.english: He spends all his time on his career.
example.fact: 事业 sits a notch grander than the everyday word for "job" — 工作 covers any ordinary employment, while 事业 implies a larger, meaningful undertaking or life's work, closer to English "career" or "cause" than a mere day job.

examples.hanzi: 她很重视自己的事业。
examples.pinyin: Tā hěn zhòngshì zìjǐ de shìyè.
examples.english: She takes her career very seriously.

examples.hanzi: 他的事业越做越大。
examples.pinyin: Tā de shìyè yuè zuò yuè dà.
examples.english: His business keeps getting bigger.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — 禾 is grain, as in 种, 秋; 稍 first meant the tip of the grain, a little bit.
肖 (xiāo) — near sound — 稍 is shāo; 肖 also sounds out 消 xiāo and 削 xiāo.

example.pinyin: Qǐng shāo děng yíxià.
example.english: Please wait a moment.
example.fact: 稍 is an adverb that needs a verb or adjective: 稍大 (slightly larger), 稍等 (wait a moment). 请稍等 is the standard service phrase, and the fuller 稍微 means the same thing.

examples.hanzi: 今天稍微冷一点。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān shāowēi lěng yìdiǎn.
examples.english: It's a little cold today.

examples.hanzi: 你稍等，我马上就来。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ shāo děng, wǒ mǎshàng jiù lái.
examples.english: Wait a moment; I'll be right there.

components.note: 亻 (person) — person radical; 仅 is the simplified form of 僅.
又 (yòu) — in the old form 僅 the sound came from 堇 (jǐn); 仅 and 谨 jǐn sound the same.

example.hanzi: 他仅用了十分钟就做完了。
example.pinyin: Tā jǐn yòng le shí fēnzhōng jiù zuò wán le.
example.english: He finished in only ten minutes.
example.fact: 仅 is the more formal, written counterpart of 只: 不仅...而且 (not only ... but also) and 仅仅 (just, merely) are common. It is pronounced like 尽 in some uses, which is a source of confusion.

examples.hanzi: 我们仅仅聊了几分钟。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jǐnjǐn liáo le jǐ fēnzhōng.
examples.english: We only chatted for a few minutes.

examples.hanzi: 这件事不仅他知道，我也知道。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì bùjǐn tā zhīdào, wǒ yě zhīdào.
examples.english: Not only does he know about this; I do too.
